items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "chromophore"?
options: The reaction of a primary aromatic amine with nitrous acid (NaNO₂ + HCl) below 10 °C to form a diazonium salt.
The electrophilic substitution of a diazonium ion onto an activated arene such as phenol, forming an azo compound.
The part of a dye molecule, such as an extended delocalised system containing –N=N–, responsible for absorbing visible light.
Ar–N₂⁺, the cation formed by diazotisation, which acts as an electrophile in coupling reactions.
items.answer: The part of a dye molecule, such as an extended delocalised system containing –N=N–, responsible for absorbing visible light.
items.markingKey: Chromophore: the part of a dye molecule, such as an extended delocalised system containing –N=N–, responsible for absorbing visible light.

(b) Write an equation for the reaction of [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ with EDTA⁴⁻ and explain why it occurs. (c) Explain why the Kstab values are quoted as logarithms.
items.answer: (a) [[CuCl₄]²⁻] ÷ ([[Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺][Cl⁻]⁴); dm¹² mol⁻⁴ (b) [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ + EDTA⁴⁻ → [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ + 4NH₃ + 2H₂O; [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ is more stable (larger Kstab); particles increase from 2 to 7 so ΔS is positive (chelate effect). (c) The values cover a very large range (10⁵ to 10¹⁹), so logarithms are easier to compare.

items.stem: Leila is studying the reaction 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g) (ΔH° = −196 kJ mol⁻¹). Standard entropies (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹): SO₂(g) 248.1, O₂(g) 205.0, SO₃(g) 256.7. (a) Predict, without calculation, the sign of ΔS° for this reaction. Explain your prediction. (b) Calculate ΔS° for the reaction. (c) Explain why all the standard entropy values are positive. (d) Calculate ΔG° at 298 K and state whether the reaction is feasible at this temperature.

items.stem: Felix is given three colourless liquids labelled A, B and C. items.answer: (a) Ethanoic acid gives effervescence (CO₂, turns limewater milky); phenol and ethanol do not react. (c) Lone pair on O delocalised into the ring increases electron density, polarising Br₂ without a catalyst.

items.answer: (a) Conc HNO₃ + conc H₂SO₄ below 55 °C; then Sn + conc HCl, reflux, then NaOH(aq). (c) ClC₆H₄–N=N–C₁₀H₆OH (coupling at the 4-position / 1-position for naphthol); alkaline solution (NaOH), cold (d) The –N=N– group links two aromatic rings into an extended delocalised system that absorbs light in the visible region.

items.stem: Ethan investigated the reaction H₂O₂(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) + 2H⁺(aq) → I₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l) in a school laboratory using measuring the volume of gas produced at regular intervals. Results: experiment 1: [H₂O₂] = 0.02, [I⁻] = 0.05, [H⁺] = 0.2, initial rate = 4.00 × 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹; experiment 2: [H₂O₂] = 0.06, [I⁻] = 0.05, [H⁺] = 0.2, initial rate = 1.20 × 10⁻⁶ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹; experiment 3: [H₂O₂] = 0.02, [I⁻] = 0.1, [H⁺] = 0.2, initial rate = 8.00 × 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹; experiment 4: [H₂O₂] = 0.02, [I⁻] = 0.05, [H⁺] = 0.8, initial rate = 4.00 × 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. (a) Deduce the order of reaction with respect to each reactant, explaining your reasoning. (b) Explain why it is the initial rate that is measured in each experiment. (c) Explain why H⁺ does not appear in the rate equation even though it is a reactant.
items.answer: (a) first order in H₂O₂; first order in I⁻; zero order in H⁺ (b) At the start the concentrations are known exactly (equal to the values mixed) and the products have not yet affected the rate. (c) H⁺ is not involved in the rate-determining step; it reacts in a fast step after the slow step.

SOCl₂, a reagent that converts carboxylic acids into acyl chlorides, giving SO₂ and HCl as gaseous by-products.
An amide in which a hydrogen on nitrogen is replaced by an alkyl or aryl group, e.g. N-methylethanamide.
A compound containing the –COCl functional group, e.g. ethanoyl chloride CH₃COCl.
items.answer: An amide in which a hydrogen on nitrogen is replaced by an alkyl or aryl group, e.g. N-methylethanamide.
items.markingKey: N-substituted amide: an amide in which a hydrogen on nitrogen is replaced by an alkyl or aryl group, e.g. N-methylethanamide.

items.stem: Tomás in Bogotá builds an electrochemical cell based on the reaction Zn(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s), which has E°cell = +1.56 V. (a) Explain what the signs of E°cell and ΔG° show about the reaction. (b) Suggest why the reaction might not be observed when the reagents are mixed, even though ΔG° is negative. (c) Describe and explain how E for the cell would change if the concentration of a reactant ion were increased. (d) State the relationship between ΔG and the cell e.m.f. under non-standard conditions.
items.answer: (a) E°cell positive and ΔG° negative: the reaction is thermodynamically feasible under standard conditions. (b) The activation energy may be high so the rate is very slow; or concentrations are not standard. (c) E becomes more positive: the equilibrium at that electrode shifts to the right (Le Chatelier / Nernst), so the reaction becomes more feasible and ΔG more negative. (d) ΔG = −nFE, using the measured cell e.m.f. E.
items.markingKey: (a) E°cell positive and ΔG° negative: the reaction is thermodynamically feasible under standard conditions [2] [2] (b) The activation energy may be high so the rate is very slow; or concentrations are not standard [1] (c) E more positive [1]; reason [1] [2] (d) ΔG = −nFE, using the measured cell e.m.f; E [1]

Jonas uses colorimetry to find the concentration of copper(II) ions in a sample of waste water from a factory in Hanoi. Excess aqueous ammonia is added to form the deep blue complex [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺. Standards give a straight calibration line with absorbance 0.65 at 0.0100 mol dm⁻³ (passing through the origin). The sample gives an absorbance of 0.27. (a) Explain why excess ammonia is added before measuring the absorbance. (b) Calculate the concentration of copper(II) ions in the sample. (c) Explain, in terms of d orbitals, why the ammine complex has a different colour from the aqua complex. (d) Explain why a solution of Zn²⁺ ions treated in the same way would give no absorbance in the visible region.
items.answer: (a) To convert all Cu²⁺ into the intensely coloured ammine complex, which absorbs more strongly than [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺, improving sensitivity. (b) 0.00415 mol dm⁻³ (c) NH₃ splits the d orbitals more than H₂O (larger ΔE), so a shorter wavelength of light is absorbed and the transmitted colour changes from pale blue to deep blue. (d) Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰; there is no space in the upper d orbitals for an electron to be promoted, so no d–d transitions.
items.markingKey: (a) any 2 from: To convert all Cu²⁺ into the intensely coloured ammine complex; which absorbs more strongly than [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺; improving sensitivity (1 mark each) [2] (b) conc = 0.27 ÷ 0.65 × 0.0100 [1]; = 0.00415 mol dm⁻³ [1] [2] (c) different ΔE [1]; different wavelength absorbed [1] [2] (d) Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰ [1]; there is no space in the upper d orbitals for an electron to be promoted, so no d–d transitions [1] [2]

(c) Allows ions to move to complete the circuit without mixing the solutions; KNO₃ ions do not react with or precipitate the ions in the half-cells. (d) Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag

items.stem: Diego plans to make bromobenzene, C₆H₅Br, from benzene in a university teaching laboratory by bromination. (a) State the reagents and conditions needed. (b) Describe the mechanism of the reaction. (c) Explain why benzene needs a catalyst for this reaction whereas an alkene does not. (d) Explain why the reaction gives a substitution product rather than an addition product.
items.answer: (a) Bromine with an iron(III) bromide (or iron) catalyst, room temperature, dry (b) π electrons of the ring attack Br⁺; arenium (positive) intermediate forms with delocalisation partly lost; C–H bond breaks and electrons return to the ring, restoring delocalisation; H⁺ lost. (c) Benzene's π electrons are delocalised (lower electron density) so it cannot polarise the reagent; a strong electrophile must be generated by the catalyst. (d) Loss of H⁺ restores the stable delocalised π system; addition would destroy it.
